chapter: Mambo, the Palladium and Cubop City
title: Sonny Stitt sits in at Carnegie Hall when Parker is absent
summary: Parker failed to appear for the Carnegie date, Norman Granz vouched for the young Sonny Stitt, who played "Tanga" and a second tune with the band.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Okay. Now, you already had recorded with Flip Phillips and Charlie Parker the year before you were playing at the Royal Roost. Did you have any featured artists with you that day at Carnegie Hall?

Well, that particular day? Charlie Parker was supposed to play with us because he got to take part in "Tanga", No. 2 or No. 1, whatever, but he got sick or he got lost or whatever, and so he still was - he was about eighteen* years old, you know, skinny like a toothpick - and you know that Norman Granz took the microphone and say to the people: "Charlie Parker cannot play tonight for us because he is sick or is," whatever.......
But Charlie Parker played "Repetition" with Neil Hefti that night. He sat in with them.
That night?
That night, and he also ....
Well, but he came late .....
Yes
.... but he say, Norman Granz said to the public...
No, no, no, you are right, you are absolutely right. I am sorry you are right, go ahead.

.... "If anybody that is not satisfied with this artist that I am going to introduce - to me and I want you to respect my opinion, not because I am a musician, because I love jazz, and I been in jazz all my life and is my
first love; if anybody is not satisfied the way this young kid play, he could go to the ticket and get his money back" - and the place was packed .....
Who sat in with you?
Sonny Stiff.
Sonny Stiff !!

.... and forget it!! That, but let me tell you, Sonny Stiff is another outstanding musician. Naturally, he start playing when Charlie Parker was in his heydays, like a genius, but Sonny Stiff is a legitimate musician. A tremendous clarinet player, a good reader, he is a good teacher, he had a good education in music. As a matter of fact, he graduated from the Boston Conservatory. As a matter of fact, last year we played a concert at the concert place in Boston.
How many numbers - not to get off the subject - how many numbers did Stiff played with you that day?
Two numbers.
Which - and they were which ones?
The other one was something that we was faking. We just got two chords or three chords and he play like he, like ......
The first one was "Tanga"?
"Tanga"
And then the second one was .....
... and the second one, I forgot the name, but I know there was something similar to "Tanga".
I see, I see, okay.
Oh!! He is fantastic.
